content: The ESC 2015 schedule outlines the coordination of TV events for the European Society of Cardiology Congress 2015. The filming location is the Crowne Plaza London Docklands, located at Western Gateway, Royal Victoria Dock, London, E16 1AL, United Kingdom. Below is a detailed breakdown of the scheduled interviews and topics: Sunday, August 30, 2015 4:30 PM: Dr. Robert Byrne will discuss the ESC 2015 wrap-up from the perspective of the UK and Ireland. Monday, August 31, 2015 8:30 AM: Dr. Vivek Reddy will present on the safety and efficacy of a leadless pacemaker, with results from the LEADLESS II clinical trial. The embargo lifts on Sunday, August 30th at 5:38 PM. 9:30 AM: Dr. Kazuaki Kaitan and Dr. Atsushi Kobori will discuss the efficacy of antiarrhythmic drugs for short-term use after catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation (EAST-AF trial) and the efficacy of adenosine triphosphate-guided ablation for atrial fibrillation (UNDER-ATP trial). The embargo lifts on Sunday, August 30th at 4:30 PM. 10:00 AM: Prof. Michel Ovize will address whether cyclosporine improves clinical outcomes in STEMI patients, based on findings from the CIRCUS trial. The embargo lifts on Sunday, August 30th at 12:27 PM. 11:30 AM: Dr. Morris Brown will present the principal results from the PATHWAY-3 trial, which compares single and combination diuretics in essential hypertension. The embargo lifts on Monday, August 31st at 5:16 PM. 12:00 PM: Dr. Luigi Di Biase will discuss the effect of empirical left atrial appendage isolation on long-term outcomes in patients with long-standing persistent atrial fibrillation undergoing catheter ablation, with results from the BELIEF trial. The embargo lifts on Sunday, August 30th at 4:53 PM. 1:30 PM: Dr. Eldrin Lewis will evaluate lixisenatide in acute coronary syndromes, based on findings from the ELIXA trial. The embargo lifts on Monday, August 31st at 11:36 AM. 2:30 PM: Dr. Dirk Westermann will discuss the accurate and rapid diagnosis of myocardial infarction using a high-sensitivity Troponin I 1-hour algorithm. The embargo lifts on Sunday, August 30th at 11:00 AM. 3:00 PM: Dr. Basil Lewis will provide an ESC 2015 wrap-up in Hebrew. 3:30 PM: Dr. Renato Lopes will provide an ESC 2015 wrap-up in Portuguese. 4:00 PM: Prof. Freek Verheugt will present the ESC 2015 wrap-up from the perspective of the Netherlands. Tuesday, September 1, 2015 9:30 AM: Dr. Takeshi Kimura will present 12-month clinical and 13-month angiographic outcomes from the ABSORB Japan trial, which evaluates the Absorb Bioresorbable Vascular Scaffold versus metallic drug-eluting stents. The embargo lifts on Tuesday, September 1st at 5:06 PM. 10:00 AM: Dr. Gérard Helft will discuss the OPTIDUAL trial, comparing 12 versus 48 months of clopidogrel after drug-eluting stent placement. The embargo lifts on Monday, August 31st at 12:12 PM. 10:30 AM: Dr. Pamela Douglas will present the outcomes of an FFRCT diagnostic strategy versus usual care in suspected coronary artery disease, based on results from the PLATFORM study. The embargo lifts on Tuesday, September 1st at 4:30 PM. 11:00 AM: Dr. Hisao Ogawa will discuss the ATTEMPT-CVD trial, which evaluates telmisartan for the prevention of cardiovascular diseases, and provide an ESC 2015 wrap-up in Japanese. The embargo lifts on Monday, August 31st at 4:30 PM. 11:30 AM: Dr. Marco Valgimigli will present findings from the MATRIX Antithrombin study, which focuses on minimizing adverse hemorrhagic events through transradial access and systemic implementation of angioX. The embargo lifts on Tuesday, September 1st at 5:24 PM. 12:00 PM: Prof. Thomas MacDonald will discuss the SCOT trial, a randomized study comparing the cardiovascular safety of celecoxib versus traditional NSAIDs. The embargo lifts on Monday, August 31st at 11:54 AM. 1:00 PM: Dr. Gregg Stone will present on peri-infarct zone pacing to prevent adverse left ventricular remodeling in patients with very large myocardial infarctions. The embargo lifts on Sunday, August 30th at 11:54 AM. 1:30 PM: Dr. Patrick Serruys will discuss the ABSORB STEMI TROFI II trial, which compares everolimus-eluting bioresorbable vascular scaffolds versus durable polymer everolimus-eluting metallic stents in acute myocardial infarction patients. The embargo lifts on Tuesday, September 1st at 4:48 PM. 2:00 PM: Dr. Frank Rademakers will present on determining optimal non-invasive parameters for predicting left ventricular morphologic and functional remodeling in chronic ischemic patients. The embargo lifts on Sunday, August 30th at 11:18 AM. 3:00 PM: Dr. Gerasimos Filippatos will discuss the ARTS-HF trial, which compares finerenone versus eplerenone in patients with worsening chronic heart failure and type 2 diabetes mellitus and/or chronic kidney disease. The embargo lifts on Monday, August 31st at 11:18 AM. 3:30 PM: Dr. Carlos A. Morillo will present findings from the Benznidazole Evaluation for Interrupting Trypanosomiasis trial. The embargo lifts on Tuesday, September 1st at 12:08 PM. 4:00 PM: Dr. Stefan James and Dr. Jonas Oldgren will provide a wrap-up from a Scandinavian perspective. 4:30 PM: Dr. Sergio Leonardi and Prof. Gaetano De Ferrari will provide an ESC 2015 wrap-up in Italian. 5:00 PM 6:00 PM: Prof. Gilles Montalescot will discuss the ALBATROSS trial, which evaluates early aldosterone blockade in acute myocardial infarction, and the AEGIS study, which assesses an education and guidance program for apixaban adherence in non-valvular atrial fibrillation. He will also provide an ESC 2015 wrap-up in French. The embargo lifts on Sunday, August 30th at 11:36 AM (ALBATROSS) and 5:16 PM (AEGEAN). Wednesday, September 2, 2015 9:00 AM: Prof. Harvey White will provide an ESC 2015 wrap-up from the perspective of the Pacific Rim.
